findings.title: Embedded client-secret assignment values cross runtime/store boundaries
findings.prediction: client-secret, client_secret, and client secret assignment-shaped values are rejected in every free-form runtime and store path before append
findings.observation: prefix-client-secret=redacted and prefix_client_secret=redacted were accepted by normalizeMetadata, normalizeReason, normalizeConnectionDefinition, normalizeConnectionEvent, and createConnectionStore; each store probe appended one event. The exact unprefixed, case-variant, and whitespace-separated forms were rejected.
findings.impact: The runtime assignment detector requires a boundary before client-secret; a hyphen or underscore prefix bypasses it, while the public schema rejects the same value. A raw assignment-shaped value can therefore be appended by the authoritative store.

findings.title: Runtime metadata width is unbounded relative to the public schema
findings.prediction: The runtime/store and public schema agree at the 64-property metadata boundary
findings.observation: A 65-property safe metadata object was accepted by normalizeMetadata and createConnectionStore, with one event appended; Ajv rejected it at metadata maxProperties 64.
findings.impact: The canonical runtime/store boundary does not enforce the public resource bound, so schema-only and runtime callers have different accepted metadata policies.

findings.title: Astral metadata strings have different runtime and public length semantics
findings.prediction: A 512-character metadata string has the same result in runtime/store and Ajv
findings.observation: A string containing 512 astral Unicode code points was accepted by the public schema but rejected by runtime normalization because JavaScript value.length counts 1024 UTF-16 code units; the store therefore rejects it as well.
findings.impact: The published schema and canonical runtime disagree on the documented metadata string limit, creating a non-deterministic API boundary for valid Unicode labels.
